Guide\n\nA small, deterministic HTTP service for D&D 5e helper calculations. It uses only Node.js 26 built-ins (`node:http`, `node:sqlite`, `node:crypto`) and plain JavaScript ES modules.\n\n## Starting and verifying the server\n\n```bash\nPORT=3000 ./run.sh\n```\n\n`run.sh` runs `node server.js` in the foreground. Creates the HTTP server, wires the route table via `lib/router.js`, and starts listening. It calls `db.initDb()` at startup.\n- **`lib/router.js`** — Minimal HTTP router. Routes are registered in order and matched by HTTP method and regex. Captured path segments are spread as positional arguments to the handler.\n- **`lib/db.js`** — Persistence layer. Owns the SQLite `DatabaseSync` connection, the schema, and all CRUD operations. Schema creation is centralized in `ensureSchema()` and used by both initialization and reset. The `TABLE_NAMES` array is kept in dependency order so the reset path can drop child tables before parents.\n- **`lib/domain.js`** — Pure business logic and validation: dice parsing, encounter XP, initiative ordering, ability modifiers, proficiency bonus, auth hashing, and shared validation helpers (`isNonEmptyString`, `isPositiveInteger`, `isValidSlug`, etc.). This is the only destructive endpoint and is intended for tests. The drop order follows the dependency order in `lib/db.js` so foreign-key constraints are satisfied.\n\n### Request routing\n\n`server.js` builds a `Router` from `lib/router.js`. Routes are evaluated in registration order, and the first matching method/pattern wins. Parameterized routes are placed before more general parents so they are not accidentally shadowed.\n\nThe router preserves the following behavior, which the cumulative evaluator suite depends on:\n\n- `GET` without a matching route returns `405 Method Not Allowed` and does not read the body.\n- `POST` without a matching route reads the body, then returns `404 Not Found`.\n- Any other HTTP method returns `405 Method Not Allowed` without reading the body.\n\n`POST` handlers receive the raw body on `req.body` as a string. Handlers parse it with `lib/http.js::parseJson` via `lib/handlers.js::requireBody`. Invalid JSON returns `400 invalid json`.\n\n## Main API / domain groupings\n\n| Group | Endpoints | Purpose |\n|-------|-----------|---------|\n| **Health** | `GET /health` | Liveness check. |\n| **Storage** | `GET /v1/storage/status`, `POST /v1/storage/reset` | SQLite status and reset. |\n| **Auth** | `POST /v1/auth/register`, `POST /v1/auth/login` | User accounts with `scrypt` password hashing. |\n| **Core / Dice** | `POST /v1/dice/stats`, `POST /v1/checks/ability`, `POST /v1/encounters/adjusted-xp`, `POST /v1/initiative/order` | Dice stats, ability checks, encounter XP, initiative. |\n| **Characters** | `POST /v1/characters/ability-modifier`, `POST /v1/characters/proficiency`, `POST /v1/characters/derived-stats` | Character modifiers and derived stats. |\n| **PHB Rules** | `POST /v1/phb/spell-slots`, `POST /v1/phb/rests/long`, `POST /v1/phb/equipment-load` | Spell slots, long rest, carrying capacity. |\n| **Combat** | `POST /v1/combat/sessions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/conditions`, `POST /v1/combat/sessions/:id/advance` | Create session, add conditions, advance turns. |\n| **Compendium** | `POST /v1/compendium/monsters`, `GET /v1/compendium/monsters/:slug`, `POST /v1/compendium/items`, `GET /v1/compendium/items/:slug` | Monster and item reference entries. |\n| **Campaigns** | `POST /v1/campaigns`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/characters`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/events`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/state` | Campaigns, characters, and session log. |\n| **NPCs & Factions** | `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/factions`, `POST /v1/campaigns/:id/npcs`, `GET /v1/campaigns/:id/relationships` | Campaign NPCs, factions, and relationship summary. |\n| **DM Helpers** | `POST /v1/dm/encounter-builder`, `POST /v1/dm/loot-parcel`, `POST /v1/dm/session-recap` | DM-facing convenience tools. |\n\n## Conventions for safely extending and testing the codebase\n\n- **Keep handlers thin**: handlers validate input, call `lib/db.js` or `lib/domain.js`, and format responses. Business rules belong in `lib/domain.js`.\n- **Add routes in order**: new routes go into the `createRouter()` chain in `server.js` in the order they should be checked. body.error);\n\n  const campaignId = body.value?.campaign_id;\n  if (!domain.isNonEmptyString(campaignId)) return badRequest(res, 'invalid campaign_id');\n  if (!db.getCampaign(campaignId)) return notFound(res);\n\n  const party = Array.isArray(body.value?.party) ? body.value.party : [];\n  const monsterSlugs = Array.isArray(body.value?.monster_slugs) ? body.value.monster_slugs : [];\n  if (party.length === 0) return badRequest(res, 'invalid party');\n  if (monsterSlugs.length === 0) return badRequest(res, 'invalid monster_slugs');\n\n  const counts = {};\n  for (const slug of count] of Object.entries(counts)) {\n    const monster = db.getMonster(slug);\n    if (!monster) return badRequest(res, 'unknown monster');\n    monsters.push({ cr: monster.cr, count });\n  }\n\n  let
